🧭 What did Columbus actually find? — 1492 to 1493.

Columbus sailed west for the Indies carrying letters from Ferdinand and Isabella for the Great Khan of China. After 36 days at sea he reached the Bahamas, then Cuba, which he was certain was the Chinese mainland. When locals spoke of Cubanacán, the middle of the island, he heard the Great Khan. On 2 November 1492 he sent two men inland: Luis de Torres, who spoke Hebrew and some Arabic, and the sailor Rodrigo de Jerez. They came back from a village of about fifty houses, where people smoked rolled leaves of tobacco. The Mongol Khans had been driven out of China in 1368. Columbus died in 1506 still calling these lands the Indies.

📊 Data: route and dates from Columbus's log (Las Casas abstract), after Morison's reconstruction. The open-sea track and the envoys' path are approximate. The fog only lifts on what the crew could have seen.
🌍 Land: Natural Earth coasts; 1492 borders from historical-basemaps (CC BY-SA).
